segments.text: Cedar Archive room review annual record. This packet contains field notes, proposed releases, signed closures and an index of the records transferred to the conservation registrar. The field procedures describe collection of evidence and can precede a final authorization by several shifts. Each team logs its work under the numbered place in the appendix. When a local note conflicts with a signed decision, apply the decision for the site and record in question. Duplicate counts in handwritten tables are retained as audit evidence. A separate appendix describes handling of photographs, which follows a different rule.

Appendix entry 01 for Receiving. The lead marked 8 sealed crates in the handoff ledger and sent a copy to the conservation registrar. The morning crew performed a duplicate humidity check and left the local barrier in place. A second observer compared the identifying marks with the original register. The storage label indicated where a duplicate packet could be found, rather than when a particular restriction ended. A canceled entry mentioned a weekday intake limit. It was kept in the file to document the sequence of earlier decisions. The receiving crew added arrival and departure readings under separate date lines so neither number overwrote a signed record.
During review of Receiving, the team noted differences between the location diagram and the supplied marker list. The diagram was reissued to show which side of the access boundary could be used by the maintenance crew. The supervisor did not approve unscheduled changes based on the diagram alone. The packet lists the original contact at the start and the person who accepted the record at the end. General advice for nearby locations has been retained for planning, while final instructions only apply to the named location. The archive treats the countersignature and specific condition as part of each final decision.

According to RD-22, what humidity interval permits transfer of the two cases?
